title: Stream big-endian 16-bit append
summary: Recovered VA 0x5cc7a0: fastcall member with ECX stream and EDX value writes bits 8..15 then 0..7 to buffer +0x08 at unsigned cursor +0x14, incrementing the cursor after each write. No calls, bounds checks, or defined return value. Separate field accesses preserve object-overlap behavior. Original direct callers at 0x5ccada, 0x5ccaeb, 0x5ccaf6, 0x5ccf36 and 0x5ccf41 confirm the register convention.
test_description: GCC i386 differential calls to accepted original: all 65536 low words with nonzero upper bits, cursors 0..78 including final valid pair, zero and all-one values, repeated appends, and writable object overlap including cursor mutation. Compares all buffer bytes and all object bytes after pointer normalization; verifies unchanged buffer pointer and exact big-endian bytes. No imports or FS registration are used by this leaf routine. Local execution passed; oracle assembly was independently compared against all 36 bytes from Game.exe. Supplied MSVC2013 helper compiled implementation under O1, O2 and O2 /Oy-; this is compatibility evidence only.
known_limits: No matching-byte claim. Complete stream type and ownership/capacity policy remain unresolved; only accessed fields are named.
Original binary layout and oracle ABI require 32-bit pointers; the portable method also builds with native pointer widths but that layout is not the original ABI.

Null, invalid or insufficient backing storage is unchecked in the original and is not executed. Fault behavior and 32-bit address-space/cursor wrapping requiring specially mapped storage are not tested.
Compiler flags may affect generated register allocation; fastcall member source models observed ECX/EDX inputs, not a claimed original source declaration.
